metadata.title: InfoWorks ICM Modeller Personality Quiz Questions
metadata.description: 20 questions across 4 dimensions to determine your InfoWorks ICM/SWMM modelling personality type

dimensions.MA: Modelling Approach - Detail-oriented vs Big-picture thinking
dimensions.WS: Workflow Style - Automated vs Manual processes
dimensions.PS: Problem Solving - Systematic vs Intuitive methods
dimensions.DQ: Data Quality - Perfectionist vs Pragmatic standards

questions.text: When starting a new network model, you first...

options.text: Focus on getting every pipe, manhole, and connection exactly right from the start
Build a simplified skeleton model to understand system behavior first
Start with key assets at full detail, then add strategic simplifications elsewhere
It depends on the project scope, client requirements, and available data

questions.text: Your typical model includes...

options.text: Every lateral, gully, and minor connection in the network
Strategic simplifications—aggregate subcatchments, key trunk sewers only
Full detail in critical areas, aggregated elsewhere based on sensitivity analysis
Whatever the project specification and budget allow for

questions.text: When reviewing someone else's model, you...

options.text: Check individual node and link properties systematically
Run scenarios and analyze overall system response patterns
Spot-check critical assets in detail, then verify overall system behavior
Depends on the purpose of review and time available

questions.text: Your approach to subcatchment delineation is...

options.text: One subcatchment per manhole with precise contributing areas
Larger aggregated catchments that capture key runoff behavior
Detailed delineation in sensitive areas, aggregated in stable zones
Determined by catchment size, data quality, and model objectives

questions.text: When modeling storage, you prefer...

options.text: Detailed stage-storage curves from survey data for each asset
Simplified storage representations that match overall system response
Full detail for critical storage assets, simplified for minor ones
Based on available survey data and the storage's significance to results

questions.text: For repetitive modeling tasks, you prefer to...

options.text: Write Ruby scripts or use Open Data Import/Export Centre
Do it manually—you know exactly what's happening at each step
Use automation for bulk tasks but manually review outputs before applying
Depends on task complexity, frequency, and team capabilities

questions.text: When setting up multiple scenarios, you...

options.text: Create templates and batch processes to generate them efficiently
Build each scenario individually to maintain full control
Template the common elements but manually configure unique aspects
Based on the number of scenarios and how similar they are

questions.text: Your approach to data import is...

options.text: Scripted pipelines with automated field mapping and validation
Manual import with hands-on review of each data field
Automated import with manual spot-checks and exception handling
Depends on data source quality and format consistency

questions.text: When updating models for new survey data, you...

options.text: Run automated comparison scripts to identify and merge changes
Manually compare and update each affected asset
Use scripts to flag changes, then manually verify critical updates
Based on the extent of changes and their impact on existing work

questions.text: Your results extraction process is...

options.text: Automated reporting with templated outputs and batch exports
Manual extraction with custom analysis for each deliverable
Templated extraction with manual customization for client-specific needs
Tailored to client expectations and reporting requirements

questions.text: When your model won't converge, you...

options.text: Systematically isolate sections and check parameters methodically
Trust your instincts—you often know where the problem is
Start with your best guess, then systematically verify or rule it out
Depends on the type of instability and my familiarity with the model

questions.text: During calibration, you rely more on...

options.text: Statistical metrics (NSE, RMSE, peak error percentages)
Visual comparison and your experience with similar catchments
Statistical targets validated by visual checks and engineering judgment
Depends on data quality and what the client needs to see

questions.text: When choosing rainfall parameters, you...

options.text: Follow established guidelines and documented methodologies
Adjust based on what you know works for this type of catchment
Use guidelines as a starting point, adjusted by local experience
Based on regulatory requirements and available rainfall data

questions.text: Your approach to debugging flooding issues is...

options.text: Check upstream to downstream systematically with calculated checks
Jump to the likely culprit based on experience and model behavior
Check your hunches first, then systematically verify the full flow path
Depends on how well I know this network and the nature of the flooding

questions.text: When explaining model results to clients, you...

options.text: Present statistical evidence and quantified uncertainties
Tell the story of what's happening and why it makes sense
Lead with the narrative, backed by key statistics and evidence
Tailored to the client's technical background and preferences

questions.text: When you receive survey data with gaps, you...

options.text: Request resurvey or use GIS interpolation methods
Make reasonable assumptions and note them—the model needs to progress
Fill critical gaps rigorously, use justified assumptions for minor ones
Depends on gap location, budget for resurvey, and project timeline

questions.text: Your validation flags in the model are typically...

options.text: All resolved—zero warnings or errors before delivery
Reviewed and justified—some flags are acceptable in context
Critical flags resolved, minor flags documented with justification
Based on client expectations and model purpose

questions.text: When project deadlines are tight, you...

options.text: Push back to ensure data quality isn't compromised
Deliver what's achievable with clear caveats and limitations
Protect quality on critical elements while accepting pragmatic shortcuts elsewhere
Depends on the project's risk profile and what's truly essential

questions.text: Your documentation of model assumptions is...

options.text: Comprehensive with full justification for every decision
Focused on key assumptions that actually affect results
Thorough for significant assumptions, summarized for minor ones
Matched to client requirements and project handover needs

questions.text: When inheriting a model from another modeller, you...

options.text: Rebuild or fully audit it to your standards before use
Spot-check critical areas and use it if it seems reasonable
Audit high-risk areas thoroughly, accept lower-risk areas with spot-checks
Depends on the original modeller's reputation and available time
